invalid.claim: B is selecting multiple small items at the store
B has selected multiple small cosmetic items beyond the original few

decisions.claim: B previously said they were only going to get a few things
decisions.reason: 'I thought you said you were only going to get a few things' presupposes B said something about getting a few things. c1 labels this explicit/E1 but the 'I thought' hedge makes it a presupposition, matching c5.

decisions.claim: B is picking out a lipstick and some nail polish
decisions.reason: Rhetorical question 'How long does it take you to pick out a lipstick and some nail polish' presupposes B is selecting these items. E2 presupposition from question.

decisions.claim: B is shopping at a location with A for almost an hour
decisions.reason: 'We have been here for almost an hour' explicitly includes B in the shared activity and duration. Direct statement.

decisions.claim: One of the items B is selecting costs thirty dollars (characterized by A as a crayon)
decisions.reason: 'Get the stupid thirty dollar crayon' explicitly states the price and A's characterization. B is the one selecting items per context.

decisions.claim: B stated they were only going to get a few things
decisions.reason: 'I thought you said' presupposes B made a prior statement about getting a few things. Correctly labeled as presupposition.

decisions.claim: B is shopping at a cosmetics or beauty store
decisions.reason: Lipstick and nail polish presuppose a cosmetics/beauty store setting. Reasonable E2 inference from the items mentioned.

decisions.claim: One of the items B selected costs thirty dollars
decisions.reason: Same evidence and same claim as c4 (thirty dollar item). c4 is more complete with the crayon characterization.

decisions.claim: One of the items B selected is a crayon-like product (likely lip crayon)
decisions.reason: 'This is basically a crayon' is A's characterization of an item B is selecting. The 'likely lip crayon' is an inference but the core claim (crayon-like product) is E1; the parenthetical makes it E2.

decisions.claim: A and B have been at this location for almost an hour
decisions.reason: Identical claim and evidence as c3. 'A and B have been at this location for almost an hour' equals c3's formulation.

decisions.claim: B agreed to go out with A
decisions.reason: 'B agreed to go out with A' is not stated or presupposed. B's presence could be coerced, coincidental, or planned differently. No evidence of agreement.
decisions.counterexample: B may have been dragged along without agreeing.
